inspection_summary.note: Texas HHSC inspections, report investigations and assessments since October 2017, updated daily.

occurrences.finding: Requirements for Feeding Infants - No Walking or Sleeping with Bottle or Cup: Infant under 15 months was observed asleep with bottle in crib at time of inspection.     This was corrected when bottle was removed from crib by caregiver.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Requirements for Feeding Infants - No Walking or Sleeping with Bottle or Cup (26 TAC §746.2419(7))

occurrences.finding: Notify Parents in Policy if Not Administering Medication: Two medications required on a food allergy plan were observed as expired at time of inspection.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Notify Parents in Policy if Not Administering Medication (26 TAC §746.3811)

occurrences.finding: Prohibited Punishments -  Associated with Food, Naps, or Toilet Training: During an investigation it was determined a caregiver squeezed a child's face in an attempt to take food out of mouth.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Prohibited Punishments -  Associated with Food, Naps, or Toilet Training (26 TAC §746.2805(2))

occurrences.finding: Prohibited Punishments - Grabbing and Pulling: A caregiver was observed on video pulling a child by one arm on two occasions.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Prohibited Punishments - Grabbing and Pulling (26 TAC §746.2805(3))

occurrences.finding: Report Situation Placing Children at Risk: A concern regarding an alleged incident of prohibited punishment was not reported, as required.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Report Situation Placing Children at Risk (26 TAC §746.305(a)(6))

occurrences.finding: Prohibited Punishments - No Harsh, Cruel or Unusual: A caregiver put her hand on the back of a child's head during naptime and pushed the child's head into their nap mat.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Prohibited Punishments - No Harsh, Cruel or Unusual (26 TAC §746.2805)

occurrences.finding: Positive Methods of Discipline and Guidance - Brief Supervised Separation: Two children were observed to be in timeout longer than allowed by age, which is one minute per year of age. The children were under 3 years old and were in timeout for more than 5 minutes.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Positive Methods of Discipline and Guidance - Brief Supervised Separation (26 TAC §746.2803(4)(D))

occurrences.finding: Responsibilities of Employees and Caregivers -Demonstrate Competency, Good Judgment, Self-control: Caregiver did not show self-control when punching a classroom wall while children were present.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Responsibilities of Employees and Caregivers -Demonstrate Competency, Good Judgment, Self-control (26 TAC §746.1201(1))

occurrences.finding: Training Requirements for Employees, Caregivers, and Directors - Pediatric First Aid with Rescue Breathing: Four out of ten caregiver records did not have current  first aid training available to review at time of inspection.     Corrected at inspection when all four caregivers completed first aid training.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Training Requirements for Employees, Caregivers, and Directors - Pediatric First Aid with Rescue Breathing (26 TAC §746.1301(a)(3)(A))

occurrences.finding: Infant Care Area Furnishings and Equipment -Use of Safety Straps: Infant under 12 months old was observed during inspection in high chair without use of safety straps.     This was corrected at inspection when safety straps were fastened.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Infant Care Area Furnishings and Equipment -Use of Safety Straps (26 TAC §746.2407)

occurrences.finding: Prohibited Punishments - Using Harsh, Abusive or Profane Language: This standard was found deficient during a DFPS investigation when a caregiver yelled and used profanity towards a child in an aggressive manner.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Prohibited Punishments - Humiliating, Rejecting, Yelling (26 TAC §746.2805(6))

occurrences.finding: AP Responsibilities of Employees and Caregivers -Ensure No Child Abused, Neglected, or Exploited: This standard was found deficient as part of a DFPS Investigation.
occurrences.violation_type_title: AP Responsibilities of Employees and Caregivers -Ensure No Child Abused, Neglected, or Exploited (26 TAC §746.1201(4))

occurrences.finding: Prohibited Punishments - Grabbing and Pulling: This standard was found deficient during a DFPS investigation when a caregiver grabbed and pulled three different children. One child was grabbed by the arm and dragged approx. 5 feet. One child was aggressively grabbed and pulled by the arm to a sit-down position. One child was yanked up to a standing position.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Prohibited Punishments - Grabbing and Pulling (26 TAC §746.2805(3))

occurrences.finding: Reduction of child/caregiver naptime ratio by 50% allowed, If 13 or more children in care, children are 18 mo. or older and other standards met: Classroom was observed with 10 children ranging in ages from 16 months to 21 months with one caregiver.     Corrected at inspection when second caregiver was added to classroom.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Reduction of child/caregiver naptime ratio by 50% allowed, If 13 or more children in care, children are 18 mo. or older and other standards met (26 TAC §746.1613(a))

occurrences.finding: Children Handwashing After Toileting or Diapering: Children's hands in a one year old classroom are not being washed after diapering.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Children Handwashing After Toileting or Diapering (26 TAC §746.3417(3))

occurrences.finding: Employee Handwashing After Diapering a Child: A caregiver did not wash hands after diaper children.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Employee Handwashing After Diapering a Child (26 TAC §746.3415(4))

occurrences.finding: Personal use of electronic devices, such as cell phones, MP3 players, tablets, and video games: On 5/2/2024, an employee was viewed on their personal cell phone for approximately 30 minutes during naptime supervision.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Personal use of electronic devices, such as cell phones, MP3 players, tablets, and video games (26 TAC §746.1203(3)(D))

occurrences.finding: Maintenance Procedures for Active Play - Hazards Removed or Repaired: The operation failed to do a check for possible hazards before allowing children outside to play on the temporary playground.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Maintenance Procedures for Active Play - Hazards Removed or Repaired (26 TAC §746.4751(c))

occurrences.finding: Policies Comply with Rules: The governing body has failed to ensure the operation is maintaining compliance and that the director is completing all required director responsibilities.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Policies Comply with Rules (26 TAC §746.201(1))

occurrences.finding: Responsibilities of Employees and Caregivers -Demonstrate Competency, Good Judgment, Self-control: A caregiver used poor judgement when the lifting a child from the floor.  The method the caregiver used resulted in an injury to the child's right elbow.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Responsibilities of Employees and Caregivers -Demonstrate Competency, Good Judgment, Self-control (26 TAC §746.1201(1))

occurrences.finding: Report Outbreak of Communicable Illness: The operation failed to report two cases of COVID 19 which occurred between 12/17/2023 and 12/22/2023.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Report Outbreak of Communicable Illness (26 TAC §746.305(a)(4))

occurrences.finding: Written Operational Policies - Exclusion Criteria: The operation failed to follow their Illness and Exclusion policy for children with a fever and allowed a child to remain in care.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Written Operational Policies - Exclusion Criteria (26 TAC §746.501(a)(3))

occurrences.finding: Director Responsibilities - Operate in Compliance: The director used poor judgment when she allowed a staff's child to remain in care with a fever.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Director Responsibilities - Operate in Compliance (26 TAC §746.1003(1))

occurrences.finding: Annual Sanitation Inspection: The opeation did no thave a documenation showing they have a current Health Inspection.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Annual Sanitation Inspection (26 TAC §746.3401(a))

occurrences.finding: Sheltering Drills for Lock-Down-4 times in a calendar year: The operation did not  document fire drills for the months of July, August and September 2023.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Sheltering Drills for Lock-Down-4 times in a calendar year (26 TAC §746.5205(3))

occurrences.finding: Written Feeding Instructions - Review and Update Every 30 Days: One infant's written feeding schedule was not signed by the parent.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Written Feeding Instructions - Review and Update Every 30 Days (26 TAC §746.2421(b))

occurrences.finding: Children's Products- Annual Certification: The opeation did not have a current Consumer Product Safety Commision Affidavit.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Children's Products- Annual Certification (26 TAC §746.4135(b))

occurrences.finding: Annual Fire Inspection - Before Initial Permit Issued and Every 12 Months: The opertaion did not have current documenation showing their annual City Fire Inspection.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Annual Fire Inspection - Before Initial Permit Issued and Every 12 Months (26 TAC §746.5101(a))

occurrences.finding: Supervision ensures each child?s safety, well-being, including physical proximity and auditory or visual awareness of each child?s on going activity: A caregiver failed to properly supervise a child when being unaware of the child's activities and not being able to intervene to protect the child's safety. This resulted in the child falling through a railing and sustained a fractured wrist. The caregiver also failed to immediately tend to the child after the child had fallen.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Supervision ensures each child?s safety, well-being, including physical proximity and auditory or visual awareness of each child?s on going activity (26 TAC §746.1205(a)(4))

occurrences.finding: Children Handwashing Before Eating: Staff stated they did not have 12 children wash their hands prior to being served lunch.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Children Handwashing Before Eating (26 TAC §746.3417(1))

occurrences.finding: Employee Handwashing After Diapering a Child: A caregiver did not wash their hands after diapering.     The vioaltion was corrected at the time of inspetion.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Employee Handwashing After Diapering a Child (26 TAC §746.3415(4))

occurrences.finding: Adequate Lighting During Naptime: One interior classroom did not have adequate lighting during naptime.      The violation was corrected during the inspeciton.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Adequate Lighting During Naptime (26 TAC §746.2911)

occurrences.finding: Required Admission Information - Emergency Medical Authorization: The ten files reviewed did not have the admissions form section regarding Emergency Medical Authorization information completed and signecd the parent.     12/9/2022 - This violation has been re-cited.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Required Admission Information - Special Needs Statement (26 TAC §746.605(12))

occurrences.finding: Written Feeding Instructions - Signed and Dated by Parent or Health-Care Professional: Six infant feeding schedules are not signed and dated by the parent.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Written Feeding Instructions - Signed and Dated by Parent or Health-Care Professional (26 TAC §746.2421(a))

occurrences.finding: Required Admission Information - Emergency Medical Authorization: The ten files reviewed did not have the admissions form section regarding Emergency Medical Authorization information completed and signecd the parent.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Required Admission Information - Special Needs Statement (26 TAC §746.605(12))

occurrences.finding: Food Allergy Emergency Plan Signed by Parents and Health Care Professional: One child did not have a food allergy plan.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Food Allergy Emergency Plan Signed by Parents and Health Care Professional (26 TAC §746.3819)
